advisory.text: GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 / CVE-2026-118773: 'Glob: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal'. npm package glob, vulnerable range >= 9.0.0, <= 14.0.1, first patched 14.0.2. Abort branches in src/walker.ts (GlobUtil.walkCB, walkCB2, walkCBSync, walkCB2Sync) call cb() without returning, so after an AbortSignal/AbortSignal.timeout() rejection the walk still reaches processPatterns/readdirCB and recursion. - GlobUtil.walkCB()
- GlobUtil.walkCB2()
- GlobUtil.walkCBSync()
- GlobUtil.walkCB2Sync()

if (this.signal?.aborted) cb()

{"source":"https://api.github.com/advisories/ghsa-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4","advisories":[{"ghsa_id":"GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4","cve_id":"CVE-2026-118773","html_url":"https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4","summary":"Glob: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal","description":"### Summary

In glob 13.0.6, an aborted async walk rejects or emits an error but continues recursively reading directories in the background.

The root cause is that abort branches in src/walker.ts call cb() without returning. As a result, callers that rely on signal or AbortSignal.timeout() to bound glob traversal cost can still incur filesystem I/O and CPU work after the request has already been rejected.

### Details

This was reproduced on glob v13.0.6 (commit e80cb38ae60d6cbff9e75f39032a994858994d35).

The README documents that the signal option cancels the glob walk. However, in src/walker.ts, the following methods call cb() when this.signal?.aborted is true but do not return:

- GlobUtil.walkCB()
- GlobUtil.walkCB2()
- GlobUtil.walkCBSync()
- GlobUtil.walkCB2Sync()

Example vulnerable pattern:

if (this.signal?.aborted) cb()

Because execution continues after cb(), the walker still reaches processor.processPatterns(), readdirCB(), and recursive walkCB2() calls.

The issue was directly demonstrated against v13.0.6. A source-history review shows the same missing-return pattern is present in tagged releases from v9.0.0 through v13.0.6.

The issue affects both glob() and globStream().

Recommended fix:
Change each abort branch to return immediately:

if (this.signal?.aborted) return cb()

### Proof of concept

Environment:
- Linux x86_64
- Node.js v22.23.3
- npm 10.9.9
- glob 13.0.6

Reproduction steps:

1. Install the affected package:
   npm init -y
   npm install glob@13.0.6

2. Run the attached PoC:
   node poc/abort-continues-work.mjs

The PoC aborts after the first readdir() call, waits briefly, and counts how many more directory reads happen after the promise has already rejected.

Observed output on the vulnerable version:

{
  "rejection": "Error: probe-abort",
  "readdirCalls": 1365,
  "readdirCallsAtReject": 5,
  "readdirCallsAfterReject": 1360
}

Expected behavior:
readdirCallsAfterReject should be 0.

A second PoC using AbortSignal.timeout() also reproduces the issue:

{
  "rejection": "TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout",
  "readdirCalls": 133,
  "readdirCallsAtReject": 1,
  "readdirCallsAfterReject": 132
}

The same test against a patched build with return cb() in the four abort branches stops immediately:

{
  "readdirCalls": 1,
  "readdirCallsAtReject": 1,
  "readdirCallsAfterReject": 0
}

### Impact

This is an availability issue.

Applications that expose globbing over attacker-influenced patterns or attacker-controlled directory trees and use AbortSignal / AbortSignal.timeout() as a traversal budget can still perform significant filesystem I/O and CPU work after a request has already timed out or been canceled.

Repeated timed-out requests can stack background glob walks and degrade worker throughput or service availability.

- GlobUtil.walkCBSync()
- GlobUtil.walkCB2Sync()

if (this.signal?.aborted) cb()

{"source":"https://api.github.com/advisories/ghsa-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4","advisories":[{"ghsa_id":"GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4","cve_id":"CVE-2026-118773","html_url":"https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4","summary":"Glob: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal","description":"### Summary

In glob 13.0.6, an aborted async walk rejects or emits an error but continues recursively reading directories in the background.

The root cause is that abort branches in src/walker.ts call cb() without returning. As a result, callers that rely on signal or AbortSignal.timeout() to bound glob traversal cost can still incur filesystem I/O and CPU work after the request has already been rejected.

### Details

This was reproduced on glob v13.0.6 (commit e80cb38ae60d6cbff9e75f39032a994858994d35).

The README documents that the signal option cancels the glob walk. However, in src/walker.ts, the following methods call cb() when this.signal?.aborted is true but do not return:

- GlobUtil.walkCB()
- GlobUtil.walkCB2()
- GlobUtil.walkCBSync()
- GlobUtil.walkCB2Sync()

Example vulnerable pattern:

if (this.signal?.aborted) cb()

Because execution continues after cb(), the walker still reaches processor.processPatterns(), readdirCB(), and recursive walkCB2() calls.

The issue was directly demonstrated against v13.0.6. A source-history review shows the same missing-return pattern is present in tagged releases from v9.0.0 through v13.0.6.

The issue affects both glob() and globStream().

Recommended fix:
Change each abort branch to return immediately:

if (this.signal?.aborted) return cb()

### Proof of concept

Environment:
- Linux x86_64
- Node.js v22.23.3
- npm 10.9.9
- glob 13.0.6

Reproduction steps:

1. Install the affected package:
   npm init -y
   npm install glob@13.0.6

2. Run the attached PoC:
   node poc/abort-continues-work.mjs

The PoC aborts after the first readdir() call, waits briefly, and counts how many more directory reads happen after the promise has already rejected.

Observed output on the vulnerable version:

{
  "rejection": "Error: probe-abort",
  "readdirCalls": 1365,
  "readdirCallsAtReject": 5,
  "readdirCallsAfterReject": 1360
}

Expected behavior:
readdirCallsAfterReject should be 0.

A second PoC using AbortSignal.timeout() also reproduces the issue:

{
  "rejection": "TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout",
  "readdirCalls": 133,
  "readdirCallsAtReject": 1,
  "readdirCallsAfterReject": 132
}

The same test against a patched build with return cb() in the four abort branches stops immediately:

{
  "readdirCalls": 1,
  "readdirCallsAtReject": 1,
  "readdirCallsAfterReject": 0
}

### Impact

This is an availability issue.

Applications that expose globbing over attacker-influenced patterns or attacker-controlled directory trees and use AbortSignal / AbortSignal.timeout() as a traversal budget can still perform significant filesystem I/O and CPU work after a request has already timed out or been canceled.

Repeated timed-out requests can stack background glob walks and degrade worker throughput or service availability.

README.md:424: | `MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_SCOPE` / `--connectionScope`                                               | `"session"`                                                                                                                                        | Visibility scope for MongoDB connections created at runtime. With 'session' (the default), each MCP session only sees the connections it created (plus the shared 'preconfigured' one) and they are closed when the session ends. With 'global', connections are shared across all sessions and survive session rotation. Deprecated: the MCP protocol is moving to sessionless, so this option will soon be removed and the connection scope will default to 'global'. For shared-server use cases, use the Atlas-Managed MCP server or build an authenticated library using the @mongodb-js/mcp-cli package. Note: on the sessionless (2026-07-28) HTTP path, a request without an mcp-session-id falls back to the shared ('global') scope so it can still persist connections across requests; the legacy sessionful path always carries a server-issued session. |
README.md:945: - **Multi-user isolation:** connections are scoped by the (soon-to-be-removed) `connectionScope` option, whose default is moving to `global` — every request shares one scope. The `mcp-session-id` header that keys the scope on the sessionless path is client-asserted, not a security boundary, and requests without it fall into the shared scope. So multiple users can see and operate on each other's connections, including any Atlas temporary database user credentials. The server does not distinguish callers. To ensure proper isolation, you can either setup an authenticated middleware which controls the `mcp-session-id` header or provide a custom scoping mechanism using the `@mongodb-js/mcp-*` library packages.
README.md:954: - Supply a `connectionScope` policy that keys on your verified end-user identity (e.g. the OIDC `sub` claim) so each user's connections and credentials are isolated — do not let it fall back to the shared `global` scope for multi-user traffic.

assessment.summary: VULN-6148 reports CVE-2026-118663 / GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f (CWE-174) in @hono/node-server: serveStatic, exported only from the '@hono/node-server/serve-static' subpath, decodes the already-decoded routed path a second time, so a crafted malformed percent-encoded request is routed as one path but served as another, skipping middleware mounted on a static sub-prefix (for example an auth check). Affected range >= 1.19.10, < 2.1.3; first patched 2.1.3; no 1.x release fixes it (1.19.18 is still unguarded). The ticket's 1.19.14 resolves in neither pinned target: the released product (mongodb-mcp-server@3.2.2) and main (6143ab6) each resolve @hono/node-server@1.19.17, which is itself inside the range, so the version delta is not decisive. Reachability is decisive: the vulnerable code sits behind a separate subpath export, the complete lockfile graph contains one @hono/node-server occurrence whose only declaring dependents, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.1 and @modelcontextprotocol/node@2.1.1, import only getRequestListener, and the product's HTTP layer is Express-based with no static-file serving, so the middleware-on-a-static-sub-prefix precondition is unattainable. Both targets are provisionally likely-not-affected on unreachable affected behavior. Caveat: the vulnerable serve-static files remain installed and unused.

Likely not affected. mongodb-mcp-server@3.2.2 installs @hono/node-server@1.19.17 transitively (inside the affected >=1.19.10, <2.1.3 range), but nothing imports the vulnerable serveStatic helper: the only dependents, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and @modelcontextprotocol/node, import just getRequestListener, and the HTTP layer is Express-based with no static serving, so the middleware-on-a-static-sub-prefix bypass cannot occur.

advisory.text: GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f = CVE-2026-118663 (CWE-174), npm package @hono/node-server, vulnerable_version_range >= 1.19.10, < 2.1.3, first_patched_version 2.1.3. serveStatic decodes c.req.path a second time after Hono already decoded it for routing; with a malformed percent-encoded sequence the router matches the encoded form while the second decode resolves the real directory, so middleware mounted on a static sub-prefix does not run. The file stays inside the configured root - a middleware/authorization bypass, not traversal outside root. Only applications that mount middleware on part of a serveStatic root are affected; public-only static serving is not.

affectedBehavior.text: Affected symbol is serveStatic, exported only from the './serve-static' subpath of @hono/node-server (dist/serve-static.{js,mjs}; package.json exports entry, verified in 1.19.18). In the target-resolved 1.19.17 the handler still runs filename = tryDecodeURI(c.req.path) with no percent guard (dist/serve-static.mjs line 78; dist/serve-static.js lines 86 and 102). The fix commit 982179278529d5673812116b042829f27794966f adds 'if (!options.allowPercentInPath && c.req.path.includes("%")) throw new Error()' immediately before tryDecodeURI (src/serve-static.ts lines 131-137) plus a regression test mounting '/static/admin/*' 401 above '/static/*' serveStatic that asserts '/static/%%36%31dmin/secret.txt' returns 404 without calling rewriteRequestPath. The guard ships only from 2.1.3 (present in 2.1.3/2.1.4/2.1.6; absent in 2.1.2), and the newest 1.x, 1.19.18, is still unguarded, so no 1.x release fixes this.

{"source":"https://api.github.com/advisories/ghsa-rmxm-3fg6-px4f","advisories":[{"ghsa_id":"GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f","cve_id":"CVE-2026-118663","html_url":"https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f","summary":"@hono/node-server: `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths","description":"### Summary

`serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time after Hono has already decoded it for routing. A crafted request can be routed as one path and served as another, so middleware mounted on a static prefix does not run for a file under that prefix.

### Details

Hono decodes the request path once before routing. `serveStatic` decoded it again before resolving the file. With a malformed percent-encoded sequence, the first decode leaves part of the path encoded, the router matches the encoded form, and the second decode resolves the real directory. The file is still resolved inside the configured root; this is not a traversal outside it.

### Impact

An unauthenticated attacker may reach static files without the middleware on their prefix running, for example an authentication check. This affects applications that mount middleware on part of the directory served by `serveStatic`. ### `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths

Affects: `@hono/node-server/serve-static`. Fixes `serveStatic` decoding an already-decoded path, where a crafted request could be routed as one path and served as another, skipping middleware mounted on a static prefix. GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f

Hono decodes the request path once before routing. `serveStatic` decoded it again before resolving the file. +
+By default, `serveStatic` skips request paths that still contain `%` after routing. {"source":"https://api.github.com/advisories?cve_id=CVE-2026-118663&per_page=10","advisories":[{"ghsa_id":"GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f","cve_id":"CVE-2026-118663","html_url":"https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f","summary":"@hono/node-server: `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths","description":"### Summary

`serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time after Hono has already decoded it for routing. A crafted request can be routed as one path and served as another, so middleware mounted on a static prefix does not run for a file under that prefix.

### Details

Hono decodes the request path once before routing. `serveStatic` decoded it again before resolving the file. With a malformed percent-encoded sequence, the first decode leaves part of the path encoded, the router matches the encoded form, and the second decode resolves the real directory. The file is still resolved inside the configured root; this is not a traversal outside it.

### Impact

The released mongodb-mcp-server@3.2.2 publishes only compiled dist files (62 entries, no node_modules, no embedded lockfile), and its production dependency closure contains no minimatch or glob at any version; the flagged minimatch 10.2.6 resolves solely through monorepo development tooling (eslint, typescript-eslint, braintrust). Current main behaves the same: the product importer resolves no minimatch, and 10.2.6 remains confined to root dev tooling. The mcpb bundle installs production dependencies only, and the Docker image installs the published npm package. The scanner's 'main' branch value is opaque metadata and was not used to select revisions.

Likely not affected. mongodb-mcp-server@3.2.2's production dependency closure contains no minimatch or glob, and the published tarball ships only compiled dist files (no node_modules). The flagged minimatch 10.2.6 exists solely in monorepo dev tooling (eslint, typescript-eslint), which the server neither publishes nor runs; the Docker image and mcpb bundle install that same production set.

the **/../ transformation clones a globparts entry and appends the clone to the same globparts array:

issue:
input-controlled growth of globParts during first-phase preprocessing, followed by quadratic second-phase processing.

the **/../ transformation clones a globparts entry and appends the clone to the same globparts array:
```
parts.splice(gs, 1)
const other = parts.slice(0)
other[gs] = '**'
globParts.push(other)
```
this occurs inside a do...while (didSomething) fixpoint loop, allowing generated entries to be processed again.

the expanded globparts array is subsequently processed by secondPhasePreProcess(), which performs pairwise comparisons:
```
for (let i = 0; i < globParts.length - 1; i++) {
  for (let j = i + 1; j < globParts.length; j++) {
    this.partsMatch(...)
  }
}
```
